title: Workspace Evidence-First Solution Research v1
goal: Promote a reusable workspace-level research-before-implementation workflow that lets any project/chat investigate comparable problems, current literature, open-source implementations, practitioner patterns, and candidate architectures before committing to a material implementation direction.
acceptance_criteria: A workspace-control-owned procedure defines when evidence-first solution research should trigger and when it should not.

A reusable workflow descriptor separates problem framing, prior-work/exclusion recovery, external research, architecture synthesis, candidate narrowing, benchmark planning, and implementation handoff.
The workflow requires current external evidence for materially uncertain architecture/model/library choices instead of defaulting to implementation-first trial-and-error.
Project/domain truth remains owned by the project repository; workspace-control owns only the reusable research/decision mechanics.
The workflow explicitly reuses known-good implementations and excludes previously failed approaches unless new evidence changes the failed premise.
The workflow produces a bounded shortlist and measurable implementation/benchmark hypotheses before heavyweight downloads, expensive runtime work, or broad implementation begins.
The workflow supports web, scholarly, repository, file, and connected-source evidence without depending on one specific executor/tool vendor.
The workflow is discoverable from the normal workspace-control root route so future chats can invoke it.
The descriptor and procedure pass workspace-control full integration/contract validation.
The originating EXTRACT redesign task can pin the exact durable workflow identity after promotion.
constraints: Do not move project-specific scientific or implementation truth into workspace-control.
Do not require external research for trivial, deterministic, or already-specified implementation work.
Do not treat popularity, benchmark marketing, or one source as sufficient architectural evidence.
Research is a decision stage, not permission for uncontrolled scope expansion; the owning task still defines what may be changed.
Separate current evidence from historical failed approaches and from project-specific constraints.
Do not download/install heavyweight candidates merely because they appear promising in the research survey.
Preserve executor portability: the workflow may name capability classes but not require one specific chat model or connector.
Keep the current accepted research-engine VERIFY implementation and production checkpoint unchanged while this workspace workflow is promoted.

inputs: observed research-engine EXTRACT redesign where external solution research materially changed the architecture
workspace-control workflow descriptor and operator contracts
outputs: validation evidence and exact workflow identity
